$sources: Sections of the Tianqing case's monochromes (Ding, Jun, Guan, Jian, Longquan): the turned outlines as the stage's sheet gives them (Docs/Stages/chenghuai.md, section 8: 'ceramics from the catalogue, turned profiles windows/SourceArt/Textures/ch_vessels.json scaled to them'), each traced from the Metropolitan Museum's open-access photograph of a vessel of its type (windows/Scripts/chenghuai_vessels.py): [radius, height] in metres from the centre of the foot, out along the underside, up the outside, over the lip and down the inside to the axis, the solid on the left. Art scales each to the plan's size (the catalogue's).

Sections of the Changnan case's vessels and the Ru basin (grade 'derived'): derived from each vessel's own photographs in the collection (assets/ceramics/<work>/, credited in its CREDITS.md) by MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py, each vessel's derivation written in its record: the silhouette against its plain ground, the camera fitted to the rim's and foot's ellipses (correcting the photograph's perspective), scaled to the museum's height and checked against its published diameter (turned by Art at one scale, the plan's height over its own, so it keeps its photographs' proportion: the plan gives its width as the section's; a widest diameter further than diameterTolerance, 2 per cent, from the museum's is a departure its record explains, `departure`, or make and Musee.Art.PaintedVessel find it), a ring for each row of the photograph, kept within two pixels of it (so fillets and lips keep their shape); the inside a wall's thickness in from the outside along its normal (`wallMeters`: a thin-potted vessel's its lip's, read from its photograph; any other's Data/Art/Ware.json's rule), the section checked to cross itself nowhere and its wall nowhere thinner than half of it. `museum` is the museum's record of the vessel's size; `outside` the section's first and last points of its outside. The wucai jar's foot and the collar's lower line, lost against the ground in its own shadow, are measured on its bottom view (a camera on its axis). The Ru basin's `feet` are its four cloud-scroll feet traced from its base's photograph, each an outline [across, front to back] stood up to their height.

Views (a painted vessel's): each photograph's camera as the derivation found it (bearing from the vessel's front towards its right, distance from its axis and height above its foot in metres, pitch down, focal length and optical axis in the photograph's pixels; a view along the axis, a bottom photographed from under the vessel, stands at distance 0 pitched -90, its bearing its photograph's turn about the axis); a further view is placed by registering its painting on the others' where they overlap, or where a bottom view sees a band all round (the wucai jar's DP342699), by registering each view's band on the bottom view's, its camera the one its own silhouette fixes (fitPixels, the rms of its silhouette's miss; the bottom view's, the spread of its rings), and composed only where its painting lies on theirs within 5 mm in every band of height they share (a view that doesn't is listed under `unused`, with the numbers); `placement` says how its bearing was found (fitted, registered, or unverified where its painting shares nothing with the first view's) and `overlaps` the share of the outside it sees with each other view and their correlation there, as `registration` measures them: Musee.Art.PaintedVessel measures them again from the record's cameras and the photographs (Art, Vessel/VesselDecoration.h, PlacementFaults), so a view turned from where its evidence placed it is found. Bands: the painted bands of ornament whose repeat is known, carried round where no view sees them: a count read by eye on the photographs, where the measured repeat (the autocorrelation of the band's colour where the views see it, at a peak, not the search's bound, over at least a fifth of what is seen, at a correlation of 0.5 or more) is not trusted or gives the same count to within a quarter of a repeat; a plain line; or the measured repeat alone where it comes within a quarter of a whole number of repeats a turn; `reading` says which. A band whose repeat isn't known, or whose count the photographs don't settle (the eye's count and the measured repeat disagreeing), is not listed, and where no view sees it the glaze is left (each derivation names them).

Stand: the carved phoebe stand a vessel stands on where its plan says `stand`, as the sheet gives it (Data/Stages/chenghuai/Hang.json, the cases' notes: radius 1.25 x the foot, 0.028 high under a vessel 0.20 tall, else 0.04), in the case's phoebe (Data/Stages/chenghuai/Finishes.json chenghuai.case.phoebe).

creaseDegrees: a section known only by its traced points turns smoothly where it turns less than 20 degrees from one point to the next and keeps an arris where it turns more (the lip's and the foot ring's edges): the museum's rule for a path known only by its points (Form's kernel, Tolerances.h, CreaseAngleRadians, from the as-built museum).

Composition (Art, Vessel/VesselDecoration.h): a view lends its colour wherever it sees the surface, obliquely too: where the surface faces its camera, its line of sight passes no other part of the vessel, and the place shows inside the vessel's silhouette in its photograph by its camera's miss (its fitPixels) and 2 px more (edgePixels, an edge's blur), so no view lends the ground beyond the vessel; its weight the square of the cosine between the surface's normal and its line of sight, coming in over 1 mm (clearanceMeters) as its sight clears the silhouette's margin and the vessel, so where a view's sight ends it fades rather than stopping at a seam. Each photograph is divided by its white: its hue that of the samples within 5 per cent of the 0.9 quantile of the lightness it shows where it sees the outside within 37 degrees of face on (whiteSquareness 0.8: a painted porcelain's ground is its glaze, most of what a view sees there; all it sees, where it sees too little so squarely), its lightness a plane in the surface's normal and in how squarely the view sees it (the glaze darkening or brightening towards the silhouette as the lamps round the camera light it), fitted to the plain glaze it shows wherever it sees it (samples whose channels spread no more than a quarter of their largest, glazeChroma 0.25, and no darker than 0.4 of its white, glazeLightness), taking off the photograph's shading, never below 0.2 of the white (shadeFloor). A sample 1.15 times its white is the lamp's reflection in the glaze, lent at 0.05 of its weight. The views alone give the colour from a summed weight of 0.04 (one view within 78 degrees of face on, fullWeight, as far round as a view's detail still lines up with a neighbour's: registration's squarenessCut): over the last 12 degrees to the silhouette, where one of its pixels covers more than five times the surface and the glaze's own shading falls away steeply, a view's colour fades into a band's repeats or the glaze, so its sight ends without a seam; the glaze is left whole only where no view sees the surface. The decoration is composed at up to 16000 px a metre, the finest the collection's photographs resolve (the chicken cup's), and at most 8192 px across (Art's WorkImageMaxPixels).

Registration (MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py, which reads it; Art's PlacementFaults): a view is unwrapped on a grid of 720 angles round and 240 heights up the outside (azimuthSteps, heightSteps), weighted from nothing where it sees a cell 78 degrees off face on to one face on (squarenessCut 0.2: its coarse detail still lines up with a neighbour's there, stretched fivefold), a placed view's overlaps with the others measured wherever both see the surface at all (overlapCut 0, as the composition sees it), its detail its lightness (CIE L*) band-passed between blurs of 3 and 15 cells (fineCells, coarseCells: the painting's strokes, not its shading or the photograph's grain); two views' correlation is measured where they share at least 0.02 of the grid (leastShare), and 0.45 is a genuine overlap's (genuine). Measured again from the record's cameras and photographs, a view's overlaps stand within a tenth of their recorded share (shareTolerance 0.1) and 0.05 of their recorded correlation (correlationTolerance 0.05): the stored section's rounding and the photographs' resampling move them by a few thousandths of share and a hundredth or two of correlation; a view turned a quarter turn from its place overlaps its neighbours by shares several times off, or none, or its painting no longer lies on theirs.
